item.title: Random Article Review #4, 10 October 2016
item.content:encoded:
I have to imagine that 682 was still somewhat novel as a subject back in 2010, though I found the huge amount of stories about it to be pretty played-out not long after I joined in 2012. "682-fic" is so prevalent around here that you could really consider it a separate genre at this point, but it's not one that I've ever really found very compelling. That's probably the biggest portion of my downvote.

I would say that this falls into the trap that a lot of sci-fi does with aliens that are way closer to humans than they should be, but I really don't know a whole lot about the race that's visiting the solar system here, and that's my chief complaint regarding the narrative itself. The viewpoint is that of an alien species, and while it's 682 that's the star of the show, I would have liked a little bit more of that alien intellect to leak into the story. It kind of does that through the reaction of the guests to what I think most people would consider to be a horrifying monster, but not enough to really differentiate these creatures or make them feel like characters in the story.

item.content:encoded:
Well… this will take a while. First, thanks to everyone for reading, commenting, and voting. To say I'm blown away by the response this has received would be a massive understatement.

Now, to the question of what happened:

Show mechanisms and other spoilers.
Hide spoilers.

First, yes, there are only three SCPs involved here— 682, 447, and 008— and I did make a few assumptions in writing this up. However, a key point that several people appear to be missing is that 447 is more than just the slime and its reaction to dead bodies.

What happened is that, during the apocalypse, 682 and 008 both got loose (among many others). 682 was exposed to 008 and fought it off (or, more likely, was unaffected by it), becoming a carrier for the prion. Eventually 682 found 447-1 and swallowed it, giving 682 a limitless supply of 447-2. Since 447-2 is so nutritive, 682 metabolizes most of the slime excreted, giving it that distinctive green coloring (you are what you eat and all that).

682 also figured out a way to take a small amount of its own tissue, let 008 affect it, and expose the "dead" tissue to 447-2, with hilarious results. It eventually restructured its insides to efficiently use 447-2 for both mundane and necrotic purposes, including as a rocket fuel, with "fuel lines" running out all six legs, its mouth, and, yes, its ass. This is how 682 eventually got off of Earth, and also implies that 682 now has a nasty breath weapon.

So, no, 682’s not dead or undead (and maybe not even alive, but that’s another debate), despite the infinitely amusing image of Undead Minty-Fresh 682 IN SPACE!

While I’m here, I’ll give my reasoning for why 682 didn’t immediately start snacking on aliens. It boils down to three reasons:

1. 682 had been drifting by itself in the inner solar system for who knows how long. The key phrase is “by itself”: no humans or any other meatbags around to disgust it. I figure 682 would find it very meditative and would be calmer that it has been in forever.

2. 682 was out of its element, as the biologist noted when 682 overshot Saturn by a few million clicks, and would try to avoid a confrontation until it had all six feet back on the ground.

3. 682 was seriously outsized. Imagine a crocodile trying to take over a big cruise ship, or an aircraft carrier, and that’s about the situation 682 was in.

‘Course, once the capture ship enters hyperspace, all bets are off. Either way, though, 682 demonstrates that happy endings are possible even after an apocalypse.
